author_reading_scope: Read the complete relevant argument ranges in two independent full-text treatments. Williams: the complete 28-page article, including §§2, 4–5 and Appendix A.1–A.2; the normalized stochastic-output derivative, baseline independence condition, REINFORCE score identity and episodic time-unfolding proof were inspected. The local theorem supplies explicit common-support, dominated-differentiation, finite score-return integrability, and finite-MDP path-law hypotheses; every general result and finite example is proved locally. No general nonlinear/deep optimizer convergence claim is imported.

sources.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, second-edition draft

author_read_locators.locator: §13.1, printed pp. 266–267: differentiable policy parameterization and stochastic action probabilities.
author_read_locators.disposition: The source supplies the parameterized-policy interface; the local definition states a fixed positive common support explicitly.

author_read_locators.locator: §13.2, printed pp. 268–270: episodic policy-gradient theorem, equation (13.5), and complete state-value recursion proof.
author_read_locators.disposition: The source proof differentiates the policy Bellman recursion and unrolls discounted state visitation. The local theorem proves the likelihood-ratio representation under explicit trajectory-law domination and score-return integrability.

author_read_locators.locator: §13.3, printed p. 270: conversion to the sampled return estimator, equation (13.6), gamma-to-time factor, and episode-level update caveat.
author_read_locators.disposition: The source explicitly uses gamma^t when G_t is the discounted return from time t. The local batch corrects the planned identity by this necessary factor and freezes theta while collecting each episode before one aggregate update.

author_read_locators.locator: §13.4, printed pp. 271–272: arbitrary state baseline identity (13.8), REINFORCE with baseline update (13.9), and variance discussion.
author_read_locators.disposition: The general zero-score baseline term is proved locally, and the B-page example computes one finite case where variance is eliminated. No claim is made that every baseline reduces variance.

author_read_locators.locator: §13.5, printed pp. 273–274: one-step actor-critic pseudocode, discounted actor trace, and bootstrapping-bias discussion.
author_read_locators.disposition: The procedure is stated locally with pre-update parameters and the gamma^t actor trace; the B-page finite MDP verifies a biased first update under a specified critic error.

author_read_locators.locator: §13.6, printed pp. 275–276: continuing average-reward objective and limiting steady-state distribution independent of the initial state under ergodicity.
author_read_locators.disposition: Retained as an explicit scope warning in the theorem's Remarks; no continuing average-reward result is claimed.

author_read_locators.locator: §4 and Appendix A.1, printed pp. 233–234 and PDF pp. 249–252: REINFORCE score identity, Theorem 1, normalization derivative, and baseline conditionally independent of the sampled output.
author_read_locators.disposition: The full Appendix A.1 argument is included in the reading; local proofs specialize the zero-score and baseline identities to the finite-MDP filtration and state baseline.

author_read_locators.locator: §5 and Appendix A.2, printed pp. 235–238 and PDF pp. 252–253: episodic REINFORCE and the time-unfolding proof for shared parameters.
author_read_locators.disposition: The source's episodic total-reinforcement argument is inspected completely. Its undiscounted convention is not used to omit gamma^t from the discounted MDP identity.

author_read_locators.disposition: Used only for algorithm context and the explicit no-convergence-claim caveat; Sutton and Barto supplies the full one-step pseudocode.

alternatives.argument: Sutton §13.1 and Williams §2 independently motivate a differentiable stochastic policy; the local definition adds finite-MDP stationarity, a fixed common positive support, and an explicit score vector.
Sutton §13.4 and Williams Appendix A.1 support the normalization-derivative cancellation; the local proof conditions on finite pre-action history atoms and checks zero-probability and terminal atoms.

Sutton §§13.2–13.3 and Williams Appendix A.2 provide episodic likelihood/score arguments; Williams uses undiscounted reinforcement, so the local finite-trajectory proof derives the discounted gamma-to-time factor under explicit dominated differentiation and integrability assumptions.

Sutton §13.5 provides the one-step TD actor-critic procedure and its discounted actor trace; the local definition fixes simultaneous pre-update parameters, domains, terminal continuation, and disclaims convergence.
Sutton §13.3 and Williams §5/Appendix A.2 support the episode-level score-return update; the local theorem and algorithm preserve the gamma-to-time factor and freeze the policy during the episode.

Sutton §13.4 and Williams Appendix A.1 support action-independent baseline cancellation; the local proof applies the conditional zero-score identity and a geometric integrable bound to a fixed finite state baseline.
Sutton §13.4 and Williams §4/Appendix A.1 support the fixed state-baseline update; the local procedure freezes both the baseline and policy during the episode and makes no universal variance claim.

Sutton §13.5 motivates the bootstrap-bias boundary; the complete four-state calculation is local and compares the exact zero objective gradient with expected first actor increment 1/8 under alpha=1/4, with each proposed update remaining inside the open policy domain.
Sutton §13.3 motivates the discounted sampled estimator; the complete finite Bernoulli expectation and derivative are calculated locally, with gamma^0=1.
Sutton §13.4 and Williams Appendix A.1 motivate the zero-mean baseline identity; exact finite calculations show variance 1 drops to 0 only for this stated baseline and MDP.
